help.title: Help
help.intro: ZipKit makes ZIP archives that open cleanly on Windows. This is what it checks, what it changes, and what a ZIP file cannot carry.
help.fixedNfc: Names stored the macOS way (decomposed, NFD) are converted to the composed form (NFC) Windows expects, so accented and Japanese names look the same on both.
help.fixedInvalid: Characters Windows forbids in names (< > : " | ? * \) are replaced with an underscore.
help.fixedTrailing: Dots and spaces at the end of a name are removed, since Windows drops them.
help.fixedReserved: Names Windows reserves for devices, such as CON, NUL, COM1 or LPT1, with or without an extension, get an underscore added.
help.fixedStrict: With “Strict” on, each of these blocks the archive instead of being fixed, as do the hidden characters below.
help.flaggedHidden: Zero-width and text-direction characters are kept but reported, since they can disguise a name.
help.flaggedCollision: Two names that differ only in upper and lower case, or that become the same once fixed, block the archive: Windows cannot keep both.
help.pathsRoot: Paths are made relative to the archive, and any path that would point outside it is left out.
help.pathsLong: A path longer than Windows allows (a name over 255 characters, or a whole path over 260) is reported. The count covers only the path inside the archive; the folder the recipient extracts into makes it longer.
help.contentsJunk: System clutter from macOS, Windows and Linux, such as .DS_Store, ._ files, Thumbs.db and desktop.ini, is left out while “Drop OS junk files” is on.
help.contentsDuplicate: A file reached through more than one input is archived once.
help.contentsEmpty: Empty folders are kept, or left out when you choose to prune them.
help.contentsSymlinks: Symbolic links are ignored by default. They can be kept as Unix links, which Windows extracts as small text files, or followed so their targets are archived.
help.contentsSpecial: Sockets, pipes, devices and links that cannot be followed are left out and listed in the report. A folder that cannot be read is reported, and its originals are never moved to Trash.
help.contentsDates: Modification times before 1980 or after 2107, which ZIP cannot store, are moved to the nearest date it can.
help.archiveUtf8: Names are stored as UTF-8 and marked so, which current Windows and macOS read correctly.
help.archiveModes: Each file’s Unix permissions are stored with it and applied when it is extracted on macOS.
help.archiveZip64: Very large archives use the Zip64 extension automatically.
help.archiveStored: Files that are already compressed, such as .zip, .jpg, .mp4 or .docx, are stored as they are instead of compressed again.
help.archiveSafe: The archive never includes itself, and an existing file is never replaced unless you allow it.
help.archiveManifest: The manifest, zipkit.json, records every file with its original name, size, checksum and times. Verify checks every file’s CRC-32 and, against the manifest, that nothing is missing, added or changed. Moving the originals to Trash verifies first, and goes ahead only if the originals still match.
help.notCarriedTitle: What a ZIP file does not carry
help.notCarriedAttributes: Extended attributes, resource forks, Finder tags, ACLs and hidden flags are not stored.
